question.problem:
| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ | $0.25$ |

Given the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ above for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y,$ calculate $P(Y\le 2).$
question.worked_solution:
If the random variables $X$ and $Y$ have joint distribution with joint probability mass function $f(x,y),$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=x) & ={f}_{X}(x)={\sum }_{y}f(x,y) \\ P(Y=y) & ={f}_{Y}(y)={\sum }_{x}f(x,y)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal mass functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

In this case, the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Let's add these row and column totals to our table:

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=3$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.4$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ | $0.25$ | $0.6$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.3$ | $0.35$ | $0.35$ | $1$ |

The marginal mass function for $Y$ is given in the following table:

| $y$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $0.3$ | $0.35$ | $0.35$ |

Finally, using the table of values of the marginal mass function for $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\le 2) & =P(Y\in \{1,2\}) \\  & =P(Y=1)+P(Y=2) \\  & =0.3+0.35 \\  & =0.65.\end{aligned}
$$
